subsystems.name: Air contactor
subsystems.role: draws ambient air and captures CO₂ using a solid sorbent or liquid solvent.

subsystems.name: CO₂ recovery unit
subsystems.role: releases the captured CO₂ in a concentrated stream for use.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: houses microbes that convert CO₂ and hydrogen into sugars or other organic molecules.

subsystems.name: Hydrogen and power supply
subsystems.role: provides the hydrogen and electricity that drive the microbes and the capture process.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: separates, purifies and converts the biological products into usable materials.

buildSteps.title: Choose a site with abundant low-carbon power
buildSteps.detail: Direct air capture and electrolysis are energy-intensive, so plants are sited where renewable electricity is cheap and reliable.

buildSteps.title: Install direct air capture units
buildSteps.detail: Large fans pull air through contactors where a sorbent or solvent binds CO₂.

buildSteps.title: Regenerate the sorbent and collect CO₂
buildSteps.detail: Applying heat or vacuum releases a concentrated CO₂ stream, which is compressed and stored.

buildSteps.title: Produce hydrogen by electrolysis
buildSteps.detail: Water is split into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable electricity; the hydrogen feeds the microbes.

buildSteps.title: Engineer and grow the microbial culture
buildSteps.detail: Strains are developed or adapted to fix CO₂ and hydrogen into sugars or other target molecules, then grown in seed fermenters.

buildSteps.title: Run the fermentation
buildSteps.detail: CO₂, hydrogen and nutrients are fed into bioreactors under controlled temperature, pH and pressure to maximise product yield.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and purify the products
buildSteps.detail: The broth is separated, and sugars or chemical intermediates are purified for further use.

buildSteps.title: Convert to plastics or other goods
buildSteps.detail: Purified sugars or intermediates are polymerised or chemically transformed into materials that replace fossil feedstocks.

buildSteps.title: Verify carbon removal
buildSteps.detail: Life-cycle accounting tracks how much CO₂ was removed and stored in the final product, ensuring the process is genuinely net-negative.

prerequisites.why: commercially deployed at small scale, it provides the concentrated CO₂ feedstock.
both capture and electrolysis need large amounts of clean power to be climate-beneficial.

prerequisites.tech: Gas fermentation and microbial CO₂ fixation
prerequisites.why: demonstrated in labs and pilot plants, but yields, rates and scale must improve.
supplies the hydrogen that many CO₂-fixing microbes need as an energy source.
existing chemical plants can convert sugars and other intermediates into plastics, though not yet optimised for these feedstocks.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants coupling direct air capture with fermentation to make small volumes of chemicals
pathway.unlocks: proof that the integrated process works and can be measured.

pathway.milestone: integrated demonstration plants producing thousands of tonnes per year of sugars or plastics precursors
pathway.unlocks: real cost and performance data for scale-up.

pathway.milestone: commercial plants using dedicated renewable power and on-site hydrogen
pathway.unlocks: products that can compete with fossil-based equivalents on price and carbon.

pathway.milestone: wide deployment of atmospheric carbon farming as a feedstock source
pathway.unlocks: a route to make everyday materials from air-captured CO₂ instead of oil or gas.
